 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 13, 2026, 12:13:47 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 The central government has issued new guidelines allowing officers in Pay Levels 8 and above to buy laptops for their official duties. Eligible officers can invest up to Rs 1,50,000, or Rs 1,80,000 for Make-in-India devices. After four years, these laptops can be kept, provided that all data is erased prior. In case of transfers or retirements, officers can retain laptops by settling the book value. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online The central government has issued guidelines for Level 8 and above employees The central government has revised guidelines for Level 8 (gazetted officers) and above-level officers to purchase a laptop, notebook, or a similar device if they are buying it for official purposes.
Under the revised guidelines, these officers can purchase a laptop or a similar device up to Rs 1,50,000 plus taxes. For devices with a Make-in-India (MII) component of more than 40%, the price ceiling for these officers is Rs 1,80,000 plus taxes.
Under the revised guidelines, these officers can keep the device after using it for four years. If they retire before the four-year period, they can keep the device after paying the amount equal to its book value as on the date of their relieving from the service. 
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission: High fitment factor vs high increment rate; how salaries of Level 5-7 employees may change over 10 years 
In an office memorandum (OM) dated November 10, 2026, the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance , said that if the employee is transferred to or is on deputation to public sector undertakings (PSUs), state government or a statutory body, they can keep the device with them. However, no new device will be issued to them if the concerned department is not governed by the latest guidelines.
The government also clarifies that the revised guidelines are applicable to all officers of ministries or departments of the central government.
The guidelines don’t apply to ministers and their personal staff (non-government staff), PSUs, state governments, autonomous and statutory bodies and consultants engaged by ministries and departments.
The government, however, clarifies that while the guidelines don’t apply to the above-mentioned bodies, such bodies can implement them with prior approval from the government.
Also Read: Higher EPS pension: Pensioners request Labour Ministry to withdraw EPFO circular rejecting exempted employees' higher pension claims 
Here, we explain the guidelines for purchasing laptops and similar devices for central government employees.
 Who is eligible to buy a laptop under the government’s revised guidelines? 
·Officers of the Government of India in Pay Level 8 (Gazetted) to Pay Level 11 (as per 7th CPC)
·Officers of Government of India in Pay Level 12 and above (as per 7th CPC)
The finance ministry, however, says that the secretary of the concerned department, in consultation with the financial advisor, can extend this eligibility to 75% of the sanctioned strength of Level 8-11 officers based on their functional requirements.
It means the laptop purchasing facility can be extended to 75% of Level 8-11 officers if it is required and after the mandatory approval.
Similarly, for Level 12 and above officers, the facility can be extended to 100% of the sanctioned strength based on requirement and mandatory approval.
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission news: Notified a year ago, 5 biggest 8th CPC developments since November 3, 2025 
 What is the price ceiling for purchasing laptops, notebooks, and similar devices? 
The OM says that the cost of the device should not be more than Rs 1,50,000/- plus taxes. For devices with a Make-in-India (MII) component of more than 40%, the price ceiling is Rs 1,80,000 plus taxes. These price ceilings are inclusive of the cost of the standard software. Here, the standard software refers to any software (operating system, antivirus software, or MS Office, etc.) that is essential for the running of the device for official work.
 Safety, security & maintenance of device 
The device will be the property of the government up to four years from the date of purchase.
The government will also bear the cost of the maintenance and upkeep of the device post-warranty period.
The officer who is given the device will be responsible for the safety and security of data and information.
The officer concerned will be free to get the device insured at their personal cost.
 What changes under the revised laptop guidelines? 
 Particulars Revised provision 
 Eligible officers Pay Level 8 and above 
 Eligibility for Level 8–11 50%, extendable to 75% 
 Eligibility for Level 12 and above 100% 
 Regular laptop price ceiling ₹1.50 lakh + taxes 
 Make-in-India device price ceiling ₹1.80 lakh + taxes, if MII component exceeds 40% 
 Government ownership First four years 
 Retention after four years Free of cost 
 Depreciation 25% annually 
 New laptop within four years Only in qualifying BER cases 
 Retirement before four years Employee can retain by paying book value 
 Maintenance after warranty Department bears the expenditure 
 What will be the book value of the device? 
For calculation of the book value, a depreciation of 25% per year (pro-rata basis), on the straight-line method, will be adopted.
For example: An eligible officer is issued a device (including standard software) costing Rs 1,50,000. The calculation of depreciation and book value of the device will be as follows-
 Formula 
Percentage of depreciation = (100/48) X No. of months elapsed or completed from the date of purchase of the device.
 Illustration 
 Date of purchase of device Date of retirement / leaving service Completed months Depreciation Book value / amount to be recovered 
 20.04.2026 30.04.2027 12 months 0.25 75% of the original amount* 
 20.04.2026 20.10.2027 18 months (100/48) × 18 = 37.5% 62.5% of the original amount 
 20.04.2026 30.04.2028 24 months 0.5 50% of the original amount 
 20.04.2026 19.03.2029 34 months (100/48) × 34 = 70.83% 29.17% of the original amount 
 Retention of device 
The guidelines say that after four years of usage, the officer can retain the issued device. However, they can do so after the concerned ministry ensures that the data in the device is completely wiped out.
 Beyond economic repair clause 
The guidelines also outline the condition when an officer can be issued a laptop or a device before four years of the timeframe. It can be issued in case of repair where the device has been declared as ‘beyond economical repair’.
Then, the officer can retain the device without paying any amount. The concerned office will also be eligible for a new device (based on the functional necessity).
The officer also needs to obtain a ‘beyond economical repair’ certificate from the original equipment manufacturer or its authorised service centre or agency company providing annual maintenance contract services to the department.
The new guidelines also reveal that when the repair cost is considered too high (exceeding 50% of the book value of the equipment taking depreciation into account), such cases will be dealt with on a case-by-case basis.
 Conditions at the time of transfer, s uperannuation , etc .
 If an officer retires or leaves government service within four years of purchase of such device, the officer will have the option of retaining the device by paying the amount equal to the book value of the device as on the date of their relieving from the service.
 If an officer is on a transfer or deputation to another ministry, department, or sub-ordinate office of the central government, the officer can carry the device to their new place of posting. Such an arrangement should be mentioned in the Last Pay Certificate (LPC) along with a copy of the bill.
 If the officer has been transferred to or is on deputation to PSUs, state government, and autonomous or statutory body, the officer can carry the device to their new place of posting. However, the officer will not be issued a new device during the deputation period in bodies where the OM is not applicable.
 Instructions for ministries and departments 
The OM reveals that for officials who are currently holding laptops, notebooks, or similar devices, as per the guidelines given in the OM dated July 21, 2023, their terms and conditions for the retention of the device will be governed as per the new guidelines.
